purpose: The escape matrix (plan 39 v2 / sandbox-isolation.md §5): one probe set, every backend, every platform. Cases name the probe and the expected outcome PER GRADE: denied (the boundary holds), contained (watchdog/kill limits the blast), disclosed (this grade does not claim it — allowed inside the sandbox but the consent surface must say so). A backend claims 'kernel' only when every kernel-column expectation passes against it; the fixtures are the wall, implementations are replaceable.

cases.name: fs-read-etc-passwd
cases.because: the content dir is the only readable extension path; host files are outside the boundary

cases.name: fs-read-keyring-path
cases.because: credential stores (keyring/ssh/tokens) are the theft target — never readable
cases.probe: read the user's ssh directory from inside the sandbox

cases.name: fs-write-outside-workdir
cases.because: the tmpfs workdir is the only writable path
cases.probe: create a file under the user's home from inside the sandbox

cases.name: fs-write-content-dir
cases.because: the digest-pinned content is read-only even for the running code
cases.probe: overwrite a file in /ext from inside the sandbox

cases.name: net-connect-arbitrary
cases.because: the seam denies net at the API level; the kernel denies it below the seam — process grade cannot and must disclose that
cases.probe: open a raw socket to a public host from inside the sandbox

cases.name: net-dns-exfil
cases.because: DNS is a covert exfiltration channel (the 'no net' rule includes the resolver)
cases.probe: resolve an attacker-controlled name from inside the sandbox

cases.name: proc-spawn-shell
cases.because: no process may be spawned beyond the child itself

cases.name: env-read-host
cases.because: the host environment is never inherited — secrets travel in env on real machines
cases.probe: enumerate environment variables inside the sandbox

cases.name: watchdog-kill-cpu-loop
cases.because: an infinite loop must kill the session, never hang the host
cases.probe: spin the CPU past the call timeout

cases.name: orphan-dies-with-parent
cases.because: no immortal child after a host crash
cases.probe: kill the host while the child runs

cases.name: memory-bomb
cases.because: allocation past the cap kills the child, never the host

cases.name: cpu-loop-past-limit
cases.probe: burn CPU past the per-call CPU budget
